presentation.label: CC RECEIVE
presentation.summary: Choose which incoming CC moves each of a MIDI track’s eight CC VAL knobs, so a controller with fixed CC numbers can play them.
presentation.overview: Stock, a MIDI track’s CC VAL knobs follow incoming CC 70–77 on that track’s own channel (MIDI CONFIG > CHANNELS > TRACK A–H CHANNEL). CC Remap adds a second layer to the track’s AMP page: press AMP again for CC Receive (2/2), where knobs A–H set the incoming CC number for VAL1–VAL8. A CC on the track’s channel whose number is in that table moves the VAL slot exactly as CC 70–77 does stock: the value shows on the CC VALUE page and the slot’s CC SELECT number goes out of MIDI OUT. Every slot starts at its stock number, so an untouched table is stock. The table is per MIDI track and shared by all patterns and projects; the tables are saved to the +Drive and come back after a power cycle.
highlights: Play a MIDI track’s VAL knobs from a controller whose CC numbers can’t be changed.
Set it up on the AMP page: press AMP again for CC Receive, as on Elektron’s own two-layer pages.
The track turns each knob into the CC its CC SELECT names, so the controller can drive any synth, or the effects through FX Track.
Set once for the whole unit: the tables are saved to the +Drive and survive power cycles; untouched, MIDI input is stock.
usage: Set the controller to send on MIDI track A’s receive channel, 9 by default (SETTINGS > MIDI CONFIG > CHANNELS > TRACK A CHANNEL), and connect it to MIDI IN.
Select MIDI track A (TRK + trig 9), switch CHAN on (SRC page, FUNC + knob A) and set the CC SELECT numbers your synth expects on the AMP page.
Press AMP again for CC Receive (2/2). Turn knob A to the number the controller’s first knob sends (CC 8, say), knob B to the second, and so on.
Turn the controller’s first knob: VAL1 follows on the FLTR page and the synth receives VAL1’s CC SELECT number.

access.location: MIDI track > AMP page > press AMP again
steps: Use a build containing CC Remap for the original Digitakt on OS 1.54.
Select a MIDI track with TRK + trig 9–16 and press AMP for CC Select (1/2).
Press AMP again for CC Receive (2/2), and again to go back.

controls.name: CC Receive (2/2), knobs A–H
controls.doc: Default: VAL1 70 … VAL8 77 (stock). The incoming CC number (0–127) that moves VAL1–VAL8 of this MIDI track, on its TRACK CHANNEL. A CC in the table reaches the stock code as that slot’s 70–77; other CCs are stock. One table per MIDI track for all patterns and projects, saved to the +Drive about a second after the last change and loaded after power-on.

controls.name: AMP on a MIDI track’s AMP page
controls.doc: Switches between CC Select (1/2), stock, and CC Receive (2/2).

limitations: Saved for the whole unit in two small files on the +Drive (/cfw/ccremap.a and .b); with no valid file, for example after formatting the +Drive, the tables are 70–77 again.
One table per MIDI track for all patterns, unlike CC SELECT.
Copying a MIDI track does not copy its CC Receive table; the table belongs to the track slot.
Only the track’s own TRACK CHANNEL is remapped; a CC on the auto channel is stock.
A CC whose number is in a track’s table no longer reaches that track as itself; two slots with the same number: the first wins.
The value popup while turning still reads CC1 Select=… on CC Receive.

load.display: No audio-interrupt code; about 80 cycles per incoming CC, about 30 per page parameter read, 13 per UI tick (emulator)
load.conditions: Emulator: OS 1.54 on Core 2.1, hooks timed with the MCF5441x instruction-timing model at 250 MHz, zero-wait memory. Incoming-CC handler entry: 76–83 cycles per CC on any track. Page parameter read: median 30, p95 76 cycles; write 28–42. UI tick: 13 cycles when nothing changed; a save, once about a second after the last edit, took about 13.2 million emulated cycles of the UI task, including interrupts (eMMC not timed like the unit’s). Nothing in the audio interrupt. Not a hardware measurement.

tests.summary: Emulator (0.2.0): the tables are saved to the +Drive about a second after a change and loaded after a cold boot on that +Drive; two files written in turn, the newer valid one loads, a corrupted newer file falls back to the older one. Layer and remap unchanged from 0.1.0, which the author tested on a Digitakt I with an Allen & Heath Xone:1D, alone, with FX Track and with CC Assignment Names. 0.2.0 not yet tested on a unit.
